guitar.evidence: Jimi Hendrix's white Fender Stratocaster (played upside-down/restrung for a right-handed guitar as a left-handed player) is one of the most iconic guitar associations in rock history.

tone.target: psychedelic strat through cranked amp, subtle fuzz/treble bite, dry mono attack
tone.profile: psychedelic strat through cranked amp, subtle fuzz/treble bite, dry mono attack
tone.summary: A fuzzy, high-gain signal chain utilizing a Fuzz distortion followed by a classic UK amp model (UK 45 or UK 50) to capture the raw, psychedelic sound of Hendrix's early work.

rig.name: Jimi Hendrix - All Along The Watchtower - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up hum and stray noise inherent in high-gain fuzz circuits.
Provide the essential fuzzy bite and treble boost characteristic of Fuzz Face style tones.
Used as a subtle tone shaper/boost for the upper mids and treble bite without adding excessive grit (optional secondary boost).
blocks.gap: The Green OD is generally too clean, but it serves well here to shape the high end after the fuzz.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the cranked Vox/Marshall-ish British tone, providing the necessary raw power and upper-mid presence.
Provide the classic British cabinet sound and necessary punch for a raw mono feel.
Slightly boost the upper mids and treble to enhance the 'strat neck/bridge snap' and brightness.
Used only if a slight psychedelic shimmer is needed, otherwise kept off to maintain dry mono attack.
blocks.gap: The Chorus can sometimes add too much 'lush' texture; it should be used minimally or bypassed entirely.

blocks.purpose: Provide the required 'light room only' ambience without sounding big or wet.

improvements.summary: Upgrade IR for more open, vintage cabinet realism.

proposals.reason: Enhance raw, open-air psychedelic feel and reduce boxiness.
